diet.note: Based on the PBDB ecology entry for the genus.

timeRange.note: PBDB occurrences: Santonian (Niobrara) to Early–Middle Campanian (Pierre Shale). Ages are ICS stage bounds (Santonian base 85.7 Ma, Campanian top 72.2 Ma), so the range is broader than the fossils themselves.

wingspanM.note: Field Museum models have 18 ft (about 5.5 m) wingspans. Witton & Habib (2010), citing Bennett (2001), give about 7 m for the largest pteranodontids and about 7.25 m for the largest Pteranodon; these figures are for the genus, not specifically P. longiceps.

text.en: Pteranodon was a flying reptile called a pterosaur, neither a dinosaur nor a bird. It had no teeth, and museum models give it wings about 5.5 metres (18 feet) across; the largest known Pteranodon reached about 7 metres. It was common in North America in the Late Cretaceous, and its fossils come from Kansas, South Dakota and Wyoming. It probably ate fish.

uncertain.note: Only stage-level ages available (PBDB); the end bound uses the top of the Campanian although records are labelled Early–Middle Campanian.
PBDB places Pteranodon in Pteranodontia without naming a family; no verified source for Pteranodontidae was opened.
